question: True or false: €10,000 growing at 7% a year gains more in years 31 to 40 than in years 1 to 30?
answer: True. After 30 years the €10,000 has become about €76,100, a gain of €66,100. Ten more years at 7% take it to about €149,700: a further €73,600. Each year's growth is charged on everything already earned, so the last decade outgrows the first three. Most of a patient saver's money arrives at the very end.
move: With compounding, the reward comes late; leaving early forfeits most of it.
ask: Which long effort in my life am I tempted to quit just before it would start paying?
trap: False, because thirty years of growth must beat ten.
reference: Housel, The Psychology of Money, Harriman House, 2020
